Wife of Ekiti State Governor, Prof. Olayemi Oyebanji, has called for stronger measures to protect women and girls from gender-based violence, ensure justice for survivors and hold perpetrators accountable. Oyebanji said that no woman or girl should be forced to endure violence in silence, adding that survivors must not be blamed, abandoned or subjected to further emotional trauma while seeking justice. The governor’s wife spoke in Ado Ekiti on Wednesday in a message to mark the 2026 edition of the 16 Days of Activism Against GBV, with the theme, “Unite to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity,” running from November 25 to December 10. She said that relevant government agencies, security institutions, civil society organisations and other stakeholders would continue to strengthen collaboration to expand advocacy, improve survivor support services and ensure access to justice across Ekiti State. The First Lady said, “Eliminating GBV requires sustained commitment, collective action and a justice system that prioritises the protection of vulnerable people”. She urged men and boys to become active partners in combating gender-based violence by promoting mutual respect, kindness and responsible behaviour, stressing that violence against women and girls must never be tolerated or excused. The First Lady encouraged survivors of abuse to speak out and seek help, assuring them that the state government remained committed to supporting them. She, however, maintained that efforts to combat GBV must extend beyond the 16-day campaign, requiring sustained commitment from individuals, families, institutions and communities. Oyebanji urged residents to make the protection of women and girls a shared responsibility, saying that ending gender-based violence required deliberate action beyond declarations and awareness campaigns.
